items.sentence: 95-100% is the usual normal range in healthy adults; 88-92% is the oxygen target for people at risk of carbon dioxide retention, such as those with COPD (British Thoracic Society).
items.note: MedlinePlus: normal 95-100%. NHS England diary: 95 to 100 (ambiguous snippet). BTS: 94-98% for most acutely ill adults, 88-92% for COPD or other risk of hypercapnic failure pending blood gases; TSANZ (Australia) the same 88-92%.

items.sentence: The pressure of dissolved oxygen; below 8 kPa on air is the usual definition of hypoxaemic (type 1) respiratory failure.
items.note: Search summary: UK NHS learning package uses PaO2 below 8 kPa; other sources the same (60 mmHg). The page said 'defines respiratory failure'; narrowed to type 1.

items.sentence: Low SpO2 on air -> Low oxygen saturation: needs urgent assessment (call 999 in an emergency, otherwise NHS 111 or the GP the same day); clinicians give oxygen to a target range, which is lower (88 to 92%) for people at risk of carbon dioxide retention
items.note: 'Below 92%' removed: retrieved sources gave 92% only as COVID home-monitoring leaflets (local, dated) and MedlinePlus (US: contact provider at 92% or lower, urgent at 88% or lower), so no UK general cut-off was found. Signposting is the site rule, not a retrieved claim.
